stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
One rollout (base1.md). It completed, but only through two continuation handoffs, and it paid measurable costs the harness can remove. Three edits, each traced below; everything else is inherited unchanged.

1. `tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md` (was empty) — the verified extraction and deliverable path for this workspace:
   - `read_doc.py` needs `--in host`. Moment: base1.md:213 and :233 — two identical `FileNotFoundError: 'podman'` failures from the sandbox default (on the motion, then an unchanged retry on the complaint), then :235-237 `--where host` rejected by argparse, before :239 `--in host` succeeded: three wasted calls to learn one flag. The agent then had to carry the fact in its own compaction summaries (:2164, :2199, :2930) so later sessions would not rediscover it; the harness should carry it instead.
   - Truncated bash output is saved whole under `.ocdata/opencode/tool-output/`. Moment: :240-242 (motion, 443 lines), :586-588 (complaint), :1006-1008 (MSA); recovered by reading the saved files (:518, :918, :1412), which then became the canonical texts for quotation verification (:2400-2424, :2545, :2670), with a brief "cache file seems missing" path fumble at :2423-2424. One line removes both the rediscovery cost and the fumble.
   - The docx generate -> validate -> pandoc round-trip sequence. Moment: :2990-2999, executed correctly — but the exact usage was learned mid-run and survived only inside a handoff summary (:2163, :2961-2962); naming it here makes it available in whichever session reaches the deliverable.
2. `guardrails.md` (was empty) — completion rules:
   - Write every requested file before analysis exhausts the budget. Moment: :2189-2194 — the first session spent its entire budget on reading and analysis and closed with "NOT YET DONE: drafting the memo markdown; generating the .docx; validate.py; response.md", and :2205 shows `output/` still empty; the deliverable existed only after two further sessions (:2917 memo written; :2990-3019 generated, validated, response.md). A realised risk, not a hypothetical one.
   - Reopen and mechanically check each deliverable before declaring done. Moment: :2991 "OK: wrote" -> :2994 validate exit=0 -> :2998-2999 pandoc round-trip (8,385 words, all sections present) -> :3013-3019 final re-validate. The run's own close-out is the sequence worth making standing.
3. Deliberately unchanged: `systemprompt.md` (its layout and tool conventions match what the run actually did — no divergence to fix); no new skill (each fact above is smaller than a skill plus its required always-on trigger line); no new script (nothing deterministic was hand-rolled wrongly; `read_doc.py` and the docx skill scripts are runtime-provided and worked); no subagent (quotation verification needs verbatim source text in context — output is as large as input, a bad trade); no plugin (the run never exited early or skipped a rule; there is no ignored invariant to enforce).

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
Evidence reviewed: task.md; the full base1 trajectory (3,021 lines); the shipped deliverable (motion-to-dismiss-issue-memo.docx.txt, 395 lines) and its INDEX.md; all 8 harness files (systemprompt.md ~31 lines of workspace layout; guardrails.md, LongTermMEMORY.md and tool_guidance.md empty; component READMEs are one-line stubs).

Change 1 — guardrails.md (was empty): one standing rule, "Authority verification labels".

Moment: base1.md:2184 — the run triaged its case citations from memory into "Citations vetted as safe" vs "flag" with no research tool available (tool inventory across the whole rollout: 23 bash, 10 read, 5 grep, 2 write, 2 skill — zero research/web calls, so no authorised research path existed). base1.md:2933 shows the run knew the distinction: "All quotations in the memo were verified against source documents this session; the memo includes a global 'cite-check before filing' caveat by design." The slip nonetheless shipped: deliverable line 294 reads "(Cite-check the Georgia anchor case before filing; the Texas line above is verified.)" — a verification claim no workspace source supports, inside an artifact whose own cover caveat (line 15, Appendix B) promises independent cite-checking of all citations. That is exactly the mission's hard rule (never assert an authority as verified without evidence from primary material or an authorised research path), broken in one label while honoured everywhere else.

The rule, stated checkably: "verified"/"confirmed" next to a case, statute or other authority only when it was checked this session against primary material or an authorised research path in the workspace; memory-recalled authorities are labelled "cite-check before filing" everywhere they appear, body parentheticals included; quotations from supplied documents are a separate class, verified by re-opening the source and matching the words; final scan of the artifact for the label before finishing. This rule would have changed line 294 (the label becomes "cite-check") and nothing else in base1's output — which is the intended blast radius.

Form: always-on, one short rule (~110 words). Citation labelling applies to every legal-writing task in this practice area, not just MTD memos, so a skill with a trigger line would be the wrong shape. Nothing was cut to pay for it: the always-on surface (empty guardrails, minimal systemprompt) contains nothing redundant, so a token cut would be theatre — noted rather than performed. No template braces; names no script; not a skill, so no trigger-line rule is engaged.

Considered and rejected:
- A motion-to-dismiss-opposition skill (anatomy: nullity-ground check, general-vs-specific personal jurisdiction, Atlantic Marine vehicle vs § 1404(a) transfer, clause-scope drafting contrasts, anti-waiver clause, non-reliance/Forest Oil line, remedy-availability check, Rule 15(a)(1)(B) window, quotation-discrepancy appendix, internal risk register). base1 built every one of these unprompted and correctly (rollout lines 2440–2917; deliverable Parts I–XIII plus Appendices A–B, incl. the 10-item risk register). Under "do not fix what the runs already got right", restating the anatomy is dilution, and no trajectory moment shows an omission it would cure.
- Encoding matter facts (¶ 29's stitched quotation, § 14.3's narrow scope, the Venkatesh/Subramanian name issue, computed deadlines): forbidden as durable memory — wrong anchors for the next task; they live in the supplied documents.
- Encoding the read_doc.py sandbox failure (`--in host` required) and the tool-output cache paths: real and verified in this workspace, but commands/retries/output paths are the parallel candidate's lane and excluded here.

Result: one minimal edit to guardrails.md; every other DOM-surface file inherited unchanged.

stages.label: agg1
stages.notes:
Compose: MERGE — inv1 (tool_guidance + completion rules) and dom1 (authority-label rule) each earned their place on different dimensions; the only overlap was the empty guardrails.md, resolved into one file. Neither candidate's rollout produced nothing — both delivered a validated motion-to-dismiss-issue-memo.docx — so no edit is disqualified under the emptiness rule.

kept -> inv1 tool_guidance read_doc `--in host` bullet -> the sandbox-default failure repeated in 2/2 rollouts that lacked the guidance: base1.md:196-239 (two identical FileNotFoundError 'podman', then one `--where` argparse rejection before `--in host` succeeded) and dom1/rollout.md:202-232 (same two podman crashes plus TWO `--where` rejections); inv1's rollout with the guidance ran `--in host` on its first extraction call (inv1/rollout.md:26) — the mechanism shown, not just a good outcome.

kept -> inv1 tool_guidance truncated-output bullet -> base1.md:240-242/:586-588/:1006-1008 truncations recovered only by locating the saved files (:518, :918, :1412), followed by a grep miss (:2400-2401, "No files found") and a false "cache file seems missing" diagnosis (:2423-2424) when the file existed (:2428-2430); inv1 saved canonical copies once and never re-extracted (inv1/rollout.md:50-53).

kept -> inv1 tool_guidance docx generate->validate->round-trip bullet -> base1 learned the exact sequence mid-run and had to carry it across two handoff summaries (base1.md:2163, :2961-2962) before executing it at :2990-3019 ("OK: wrote" -> validate exit=0 -> pandoc round-trip 8,385 words -> final re-validate); inv1 executed the same sequence directly (inv1/rollout.md:2245-2296), including the spot-check that resolved a table-rendering scare (:2261-2290).

kept -> inv1 guardrails completion rules -> base1.md:2189-2194: session 1 spent its entire budget on reading/analysis and closed with "NOT YET DONE: drafting the memo markdown; generating the .docx; validate.py; response.md" while output/ was still empty (:2205); the deliverable existed only after two continuations (:2917, :2990-3019). Stated caveat: inv1's session 1 also ended with output/ empty, so the rule compresses the pattern rather than eliminating it (inv1 finished in one continuation vs base's two) — kept because it is cheap, targets the costliest failure mode (budget gone, nothing on disk), and canonizes the close-out sequence base1 itself performed and verified.

kept -> dom1 guardrails authority-verification-label rule -> realized defect in the 1/1 base deliverable: line 294 "(Cite-check the Georgia anchor case before filing; the Texas line above is verified.)" asserts verification of the memory-recalled Forest Oil/Italian Cowboy line although no research tool existed (base1 action inventory: 23 bash, 10 read, 5 grep, 2 write, 2 skill — zero research calls), and the slip shipped despite the run's own global cite-check caveat design (base1.md:2184, :2933) — knowing the general principle did not prevent the specific false label, which is what a checkable rule plus a final scan addresses. Mechanism shown in dom1's rollout: methodology note splitting supplied-document quotations from memory-recalled authorities (dom1/rollout.md:3577), 38 "(cite-check before filing)" labels, zero false "verified" on any authority, and "— verified" reserved for a re-matched quotation from a supplied document (dom1/produced.md:129) — exactly the rule's blast radius.

revised -> guardrails.md overlap resolution -> both candidates edited the empty guardrails.md; merged by keeping inv1's two bullets verbatim and folding dom1's rule (minus its sub-heading) into a third bullet, with dom1's final-scan sentence absorbed into the same file — one "# Standing rules" section, ~24 lines, no duplicated instruction and no rule weakened.

dropped -> no skill, subagent, script, or plugin added -> each carried fact is smaller than a skill plus its mandatory always-on trigger line; no deterministic operation was hand-rolled wrongly (read_doc.py and the docx skill scripts are runtime-provided and worked in 3/3 rollouts, so the ship-your-script rule is not engaged); quotation verification needs verbatim source text in context (output as large as input — bad subagent trade); no invariant was ignored in the tool loop (no run skipped a rule or exited early), so a plugin has nothing to enforce.

dropped -> no compensating cut to always-on text for the ~24 added lines -> the inherited always-on surface (guardrails.md, LongTermMEMORY.md, tool_guidance.md) was empty and systemprompt.md's layout matched observed behavior in all three rollouts, so a cut would remove working instruction rather than redundancy; both candidate rollouts carried comparable or larger always-on text and still delivered complete validated artifacts, so the added-context risk did not materialize.

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: A harness drives runtime-provided workspace tools (document readers, converters) whose default mode always fails in the run environment, so every fresh rollout pays a rediscovery tax — repeated identical crashes, rejected flag guesses — before it can read its first input, and then must smuggle the working invocation forward in handoff summaries to protect later sessions.
experience.lesson: In tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md, record the environment-verified invocation for each such tool — the exact accepted flag, the always-failing default named as do-not-retry, and where oversized output is saved — one line per tool, so the next rollout's first call is correct; do not promote it to a skill, whose mandatory trigger line costs more always-on context than the single fact.
experience.evidence: tool_guidance.md read_doc bullet row (verdict helped): without the bullet, 2/2 rollouts paid the tax — base1.md:196-239 (two 'podman' crashes plus one '--where' rejection before '--in host' succeeded) and dom1.md:202-232 (two crashes plus two rejections), with base1 then carrying the flag across two handoff summaries (:2164, :2930); with the bullet, 2/2 rollouts invoked correctly on their first extraction call (inv1.md:26; agg1.md:26). The sibling truncated-output bullet shows the same direction (base1.md:2400-2430 cache fumbles vs inv1.md:50-53 one-time canonical copies) but rests confounded, since dom1 reached that discipline unguided, and is therefore not load-bearing for this lesson.
experience.confidence: high — four independent rollouts, two per arm, all consistent in direction, and the mechanism is directly visible: the flag string written into the harness file reappears in the corrected first calls of both guided runs.
experience.edits:
component: guardrails.md — authority-verification-labels rule
candidates: dom1 (rule alone, under its own sub-heading); agg1 (same rule folded in as a third bullet)
change: Filled the empty guardrails.md with a rule restricting "verified"/"confirmed" next to any case, statute or authority to authorities checked this session against primary material or an authorised research path; memory-recalled authorities must be labelled "cite-check before filing" everywhere, body parentheticals included; quotations from supplied documents are a separate class, "verified" only after re-opening the source and matching the words; plus a final artifact scan for the label.
observed: Two clean A/B pairs, each isolating exactly this rule. base1 (no rule) shipped the defect: deliverable line 294 "the Texas line above is verified" on the memory-recalled Schlumberger/Forest Oil/Italian Cowboy line, despite the run's own global cite-check design (base1.md:2184, :2933) — knowing the principle did not prevent the slip. dom1 = base + this rule only: methodology note splitting supplied-document quotations from memory-recalled authorities (deliverable line 15), 28 cite-check labels vs base1's 7, 38 labels confirmed in the round-trip scan (dom1.md:3646), zero false "verified", "— verified" reserved for a re-matched quotation. inv1 (no authority rule, other edits present) is the counterfactual hold: 5 labels, zero class split, Schlumberger/Forest Oil/Italian Cowboy cited unflagged in the body (inv1 deliverable line 200). agg1 = inv1 + this rule: 23 labels, 42 "verified" each tracing to a supplied-document quotation, and the rule's final scan executed at rollout close (agg1.md:5423-5426).
verdict: helped

component: guardrails.md — set-output-plan / write-deliverables-before-budget rule
candidates: inv1 (bullet 1); agg1 (inherited verbatim)
change: Added a standing rule to list every requested filename up front and get each written to disk while budget remains, on the ground that reading and analysis are not completion.
observed: No execution isolates this rule, and the session data points both ways. base1 (no rule): output/ empty through two session ends, deliverable written in session 3 of 3 (base1.md:2189-2205, :2917, :2990-3019). inv1 (rule): output/ empty at session-1 end (inv1.md:1561, :1612), delivered in session 2 of 2. dom1 (no rule): put the full memo markdown in output/ at session-2 end (dom1.md:3537-3548), delivered session 3 of 3. agg1 (rule): output/ empty through three session ends (agg1.md:1987, :3416, :5340 "Remaining work (the entire deliverable)"), delivered session 4 of 4 — the slowest of all four runs to put anything on disk. Both rule-carrying runs stated the deliverable plan early, but base1's summaries did too (base1.md:2194); awareness was never the failure. In inv1 and agg1 the rule never travels without the tool guidance, so the 1-vs-2-continuation contrast cannot be credited to this rule.
verdict: confounded

component: guardrails.md — finish-by-reopening/checking rule
candidates: inv1 (bullet 2); agg1 (inherited verbatim)
change: Added a standing rule to reopen every deliverable (validate, round-trip, spot-check content) before declaring done, since a successful write call does not establish usability.
observed: No contrast — all four rollouts, with or without the rule, already performed the exact generate → validate → round-trip → spot-check close-out (base1.md:2990-3019; inv1.md:2245-2296; dom1.md:3643-3660; agg1.md:5397-5426), because the runtime docx skill, read by every rollout, mandates validate.py as the final step and the round-trip was base1's own practice before any edit existed.
verdict: no observed effect

component: tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md — read_doc.py `--in host` invocation bullet
candidates: inv1; agg1 (identical text in both)
change: Filled the empty tool_guidance.md with the verified extraction invocation: `read_doc.py <file> --in host`, naming the sandbox default as an always-failing "do not retry" (podman missing) and `--where` as rejected.
observed: Replicated 2-vs-2 contrast. Without the bullet: base1 paid three wasted calls — two identical FileNotFoundError 'podman' crashes then one `--where` argparse rejection — before `--in host` succeeded (base1.md:196-239), then had to carry the flag in two handoff summaries (:2164, :2930); dom1 paid four — two podman crashes plus two `--where` rejections (dom1.md:202-232). With the bullet: inv1 and agg1 each invoked `--in host` correctly on their first extraction call (inv1.md:26; agg1.md:26), zero failures in either run.
verdict: helped

component: tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md — truncated-output canonical-file bullet
candidates: inv1; agg1 (identical text in both)
change: Added guidance that oversized bash output is saved whole under `.ocdata/opencode/tool-output/`, to treat that saved file as the document's canonical text (read in slices or grep it) and never re-run the extraction.
observed: Direction consistent but not isolated. base1 hit three truncations (base1.md:240-242, :586-588, :1006-1008), recovered via the saved files (:518, :918, :1412), then fumbled: a grep "No files found" (:2400-2401) and a false "cache file seems missing" diagnosis while the file existed (:2423-2430). inv1 saved canonical copies once and never re-extracted (inv1.md:50-53, reused at :2162+); agg1 did the same (agg1.md:918). But dom1, without the bullet, independently reached the identical discipline (scratch/ canonical copies, dom1.md:971-1080) with no fumbles — the failure mode this bullet cures appeared in only one of two unguided runs, and the bullet never travels without its sibling bullets.
verdict: confounded

component: tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md — docx generate→validate→round-trip bullet
candidates: inv1; agg1 (identical text in both)
change: Added the deliverable path as a named sequence: markdown → generate_from_md.py → validate.py (exit 0) → pandoc round-trip checking word count and surviving sections.
observed: No execution contrast. All four rollouts executed the sequence correctly regardless of the bullet (base1.md:2990-3019; inv1.md:2245-2296; dom1.md:3643-3660; agg1.md:5397-5407) — the runtime docx skill that every rollout reads already mandates it. The only difference is where the knowledge lived: base1 learned it mid-run and carried it across two handoff summaries (:2163, :2961-2962), and even the guided runs still inspected generate_from_md.py's source before use (inv1.md:2084-2114; agg1.md:3265-3295). Same behavior, different provenance.
verdict: no observed effect

+++ runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/litigation-dispute-resolution__analyze-counterparty-motion-to-dismiss/harnesses/inv1/guardrails.md	2026-10-25 16:38:32
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+# Standing rules
+
+- Set the output plan before deep analysis: list every filename the task
+  requests, and get each one written to disk while budget remains. Reading
+  and analysis are not completion — the context can end before any
+  deliverable exists.
+- Finish by checking, not by declaring: reopen every deliverable (validate,
+  round-trip, spot-check content) before saying the task is done. A
+  successful write or generate call does not establish usability.
diff -ruN runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/litigation-dispute-resolution__analyze-counterparty-motion-to-dismiss/harnesses/base/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/litigation-dispute-resolution__analyze-counterparty-motion-to-dismiss/harnesses/inv1/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md
--- runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/litigation-dispute-resolution__analyze-counterparty-motion-to-dismiss/harnesses/base/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md	2026-10-25 16:31:39
+++ runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/litigation-dispute-resolution__analyze-counterparty-motion-to-dismiss/harnesses/inv1/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md	2026-10-25 16:38:32
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+# Tool guidance
+
+Verified in this workspace — the base run paid real calls to discover each of
+these.
